analysis:
Examined units cover base ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift 1045-1694 and head 1-551. Per file_changes, the security-relevant change is an add-on hold load fence (TB-012/A-018/T-059).

Head 396-397: `addonHoldLoadRefusal(for:)` runs synchronously immediately before `isLoadingAny = true` (398). It throws before the load gate, the deviceActivity begin, the pending-load claim and the modelsLoading insert, so no gate, lease or waiter is leaked. The only registered cleanup is `defer glmOwnership?.release()` (393), which still runs. This is consistent with T-059's goal that models are not loaded beside running VMs.

Head 576-577: a second fence follows the hashing suspension and precedes the pendingLoad recheck and shard allocation. Its cleanup path (pendingLoad lease release in the outer catch) is outside the visible lines and should be confirmed in integration.

Head 711/714 (not visible here): `modelLoadInterruption(modelId)` replaces the `isShuttingDown || Task.isCancelled` check and rethrows a typed interruption. Integration should confirm three things:
- it still includes shutdown and cancellation;
- `newcomer.releaseAfterExternalResources` precedes the throw;
- the thrown error maps through `loadErrorStatusCode` to a retriable 503 and not 500. A 500 would count as a provider fault.

Base 1190-1191 (head 1202-1203) concerns the persisted-serving-set skip for `servingDrain.owner == .addonHold`. This is an availability-only change; the head side was not visible.

The weight-hash capture/publish logic (head 25-182) appears unchanged per the range map. It is fail-closed: a pre/post hash mismatch aborts before slot install, and an unavailable hash clears the advertised and live hashes (T-041, T-027).

No encryption, attestation or authorization paths changed in the visible source. The implementations of `addonHoldLoadRefusal`, `modelLoadInterruption` and the hold socket signature/lease checks were not supplied. No regression was identified.
